title: Connect a vision provider (OpenCode Zen)
purpose: Enable image input. This repo ships deepseek-only config, so Zen vision models fail until authenticated.
note: Manual, needs an interactive terminal with browser access (not inside docker exec): run opencode, type /connect, choose OpenCode Zen, complete sign-in/billing, paste the key, then /models and pick Muse Spark 1.3 Free (or MiMo-V2.6-Flash Free). Verify names-only with: python3 -c 'import json,os;print(sorted(json.load(open(os.path.expanduser("~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json")))))'. Then restart the web container; web-entrypoint merges deepseek without wiping Zen. Avoid pasting screenshots that contain secrets to Free-tier models.

title: Rotate server password
purpose: Replace OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD (its live value was echoed by docker compose config).
note: Manual: paste the generated line over the OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD line in .env.local (mode 0600), then reload and verify.

title: Deploy LiteLLM (hard cost caps)
purpose: Run the LiteLLM proxy in front of DeepSeek to enforce max_budget and get a unified cost view.
note: Proxy listens on http://127.0.0.1:4000. To route the agent through it, point opencode.json baseURL at http://127.0.0.1:4000/v1.

title: Self-host Laya + A/B vs Jev
purpose: Stand up the open-weights Jev-compatible server, then diff the same payload against TypeSafe Jev.
note: Manual: laya-serve is long-running; run it in its own terminal (POST /v1/systemone on http://127.0.0.1:8000), then run the A/B test.

title: Rotate API keys (DeepSeek + Jev)
purpose: Guided browser rotation of DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and JEV_API_KEY, then recreate and smoke-test.
note: Manual: completes browser steps at platform.deepseek.com and console.typesafe.ai, then writes .env.local and recreates the container.

title: Health check
purpose: Full health gate; --full (Tier 9) runs the Jev functional proof and (Tier 10) the repo gates (test-hygiene + test-patterns).

title: Config audit (actual vs expected)
purpose: Diff live settings against expected; lists a remediation hint per drift.
note: Also runs server-side for the dashboard config card.

title: Cost / balance / Jev count
purpose: DeepSeek balance + per-session cost from the DB + Jev invocation count.
note: Input tokens (context) are the cost driver.

title: Rebuild the search index
purpose: Build the on-disk FTS5 index over session parts (data/search/). The dashboard builds the same index in memory on demand.
note: Ranked cross-session search over text, reasoning, and tool commands. Also live in the dashboard search box.

title: Read a screenshot locally (OCR fallback)
purpose: Extract text from an image without any API model, using tesseract (preferred) or PaddleOCR (receipts-ocr backend).
note: Fallback when image input is unavailable or a model rejects it. tesseract.js (npm, pinned in package.json) works out of the box; tesseract CLI (apt, in image) and PaddleOCR (pip) also supported.

title: Blacklist guard: pause or resume
purpose: The execution-time guard blocks sed / rm -rf / subprocess.run and strips 2>/dev/null from the agent's own bash calls so stderr (the proof) is visible. Pause it if it misbehaves.
note: Manual: set OPENCODE_BLACKLIST_GUARD in .env.local (mode 0600) to block (default) | warn | off, then restart opencode-web. warn logs every match without blocking; off disables the guard. Restarting opencode-web also blips the dashboard on :5099 for a few seconds and ends the current agent session.

title: Top up the DeepSeek balance
purpose: The provider balance funds the agent. Check it before the account runs dry, then add credit.
note: Manual: cost.sh prints the DeepSeek balance (section T2) from https://api.deepseek.com/user/balance. Add credit at https://platform.deepseek.com, then re-run cost.sh to confirm. Keep the agent on deepseek-flash to slow the drain (see HANDOFF.md "Cost model").

title: Learn from the logs (issues -> proven fixes)
purpose: Mine the chat database for recurring errors and the command that fixed each, proven by the tool logs.
note: Read-only, local, no model call. Pairs each error tool call with the next completed call in the same session and ranks the recurring (issue, fix) pairs.

title: Diagnose: aggregate telemetry
purpose: Pull the real evidence (guard actions, tool errors + stack traces, events, app log, container log) instead of guessing from a slow step.
note: Read-only. 'system' and 'packet' need the host (no docker in the container). Guard actions appear after opencode-web restarts to load the plugin; they are also shown on /explore > signals.

title: Harness: whole-state check
purpose: One command for every gate + live telemetry + cost headline + the TODO in-flight list, with an optional timestamped report.
note: Robust: a failing gate is reported and the run continues; a missing gate is SKIP. --fast skips the slow dashboard gate; --export writes logs/harness-<UTC>.md. test-dashboard.sh already runs lint.sh and test-hygiene.sh.

title: Pre-flight: spend gate (fail closed)
purpose: Cheap local check that must pass before any paid session: keys, last gate result, balance, model. Fails closed so API spend stops until resolved.
note: Run harness.sh first: it records data/observability/last-gate.json, which preflight reads. preflight also reads the DeepSeek balance (one free GET). MIN_BALANCE env overrides the $1.00 floor; --allow-pro skips the model checks.

title: UX test (Playwright, host)
purpose: Assert the observability UI is usable: no console errors, no horizontal scroll at 390px, tabs toggle, and the overview stays compact.
commands: pip install playwright && playwright install chromium
note: Host-side only (the container has no browser). The dashboard must be up on 5099 (web.sh or dashboard.sh). --check reports playwright/chromium/server readiness with the exact install commands; without a browser the test prints SKIP (not a pass). Screenshots land in logs/ux/.

title: UX trace (every click/drag/scroll logged, host)
purpose: Prove the UX journey, not just assert it: injects a recorder so every click, drag and scroll is logged with the element and coordinates, enumerates interactive hotspots with bounding boxes + an overlay screenshot, and persists runs/events/hotspots/findings to data/observability/ux.db.
commands: pip install playwright && playwright install chromium
note: Host-side only. Writes screenshots + hotspots + a handoff report to logs/ux/ and structured rows to data/observability/ux.db (ux_run/ux_event/ux_hotspot/ux_finding) so a handoff reads the database instead of re-running. --self-test runs offline with no browser.

title: Connect Google Gemini
purpose: Add Gemini as an OpenAI-compatible provider so it appears in /models and the /models policy page.
commands: # create a key at https://aistudio.google.com/apikey, then add a line to .env.local (mode 0600):
note: Manual: paste the key. Gemini goes through @ai-sdk/openai-compatible at https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/. Then pick it with /models (TUI) or `opencode run -m gemini/gemini-2.5-flash`. gemini-2.5-flash and gemini-2.5-flash-lite are allow-listed in models.policy.json (Flash input is ~$0.30/1M, above the $0.20 ceiling — allowed explicitly).

title: CDP probe (:4096 vs :5099 end to end)
purpose: Prove the chain the dashboard visualizes: attach to the live browser over CDP, take session ids from the :4096 opencode API and the :5099 dashboard API, and take the rendered row ids from the live :5099 tab. PASS when the visualization is faithful to its source; dashboard-vs-opencode id drift is reported as a note. Screenshots + JSON land in logs/cdp/ (gitignored).
note: Needs a browser with remote debugging (browser-use Chrome exposes it; else set CDP_PORT). OPENCODE_SERVER_PASSWORD enables the :4096 count and is never printed. Without a browser the probe prints SKIP, which is not PASS.

title: Host recovery: docker daemon + crash-loop harness + CPU oversubscription + stale proxies
purpose: The ws24 lockup (2026-10-16): CPU oversubscription from Chrome + the crash-looping deepseek-harness service + the host opencode TUI + the :4096 web server at once. Also covers the docker daemon being disabled and stale docker-proxy holding :4096/:5099.
note: Manual, host only (needs sudo + docker + systemctl --user). ORDER: (1) enable --now docker (it was disabled, so it never survived a reboot); (2) stop/disable the crash-looping deepseek-harness.service, or bound it with CPUQuota=25%; (3) reduce co-tenants - do NOT run host TUI + :4096 web + dsh + Chrome-heavy at once on 8 cores; (4) only if `ss` shows a stale docker-proxy still holding :4096/:5099 after a stop, `sudo systemctl restart docker`. A 502 from web.sh means caddy is up but opencode-web is not answering on :4096 yet - health pre-warm takes ~25s, so retry, and read ./scripts/web-logs.sh if it persists (contention can delay boot).

title: Adopt durable-pi (device-owned agent network)
purpose: Run disler/durable-pi as a PARALLEL host service (Node 24 + OpenRouter), not a migration. See docs/durable-pi-adoption.md for the decision gate + caveats.
note: Parallel, not a migration: opencode sessions are not importable into pi-durable. Needs Node 24, just, zsh, an OpenRouter key. Their caveats: durable = checkpointed not exactly-once; a token is a shell; LAN http is cleartext; the hub holds every token; experimental (pins 1.0.3).

title: Ops: Grafana, sentinel timer + alerting, caddy TLS, media
purpose: Host-side ops for the observability stack: bring :5099 to HEAD, install the sentinel timer + NOTIFY_WEBHOOK (alerting fires), stand up Grafana+SQLite, cut the caddy TLS cost, and convert the tour to mp4.
commands: docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.observability.yml up -d   # Grafana on :3000
bash scripts/sentinel-install.sh   # user timer; unit loads .env.local
bash scripts/host-path-probe.sh   # confirms the hop is TLS-dominated
ffmpeg -i docs/ux/tour.webm docs/ux/tour.mp4   # if ffmpeg is installed
note: Grafana dashboard 'opencode — cost, sessions, flags' is provisioned (docker/grafana/provisioning/dashboards/opencode.json; datasources in ../datasources/sqlite.yaml). Sentinel timer: sentinel-install.sh writes the user unit, which loads .env.local (EnvironmentFile), so NOTIFY_WEBHOOK makes sentinel.sh call notify.sh on a trip. Caddy TLS: host-path-probe shows the hop is TLS-dominated — HTTP/2 + keep-alive are Caddy defaults; the usual fix is host CPU headroom (the lockup was CPU oversubscription). Media: panels-tour.py captures; convert webm->mp4 with ffmpeg if present.

title: Slow fetches: queue-wait on the single-threaded servers
purpose: Turn sentinel T4 'N slow fetches' into a fix. The `duration` in the caddy access log is time-in-system (queue wait + service), not handler cost: both opencode-web (:4096) and the dashboard (:5099) are single-threaded Node, so when one handler blocks the loop every queued request inflates (M/M/1: wait ~ rho/(1-rho)). Diagnose in order, then fix at the source.
commands: python3 scripts/triage-alerts.py   # group the pushed slow fetches by URI
bash scripts/host-path-probe.sh   # host -> caddy -> container: TLS vs queue
bash scripts/latency-timeline.sh --session <sid>   # agentic loop vs slow fetches
docker compose --project-directory docker restart caddy   # after editing docker/Caddyfile
note: URI histogram from the real ledger (2026-10-14..16): /provider x188 (worst 137s, per-page-load), /api/balance x13 (307s), /api/cost 365s, /api/schema 112s, /assets/* x23, /favicon x46. Two drains, both durable: (1) the servers are single-threaded -> keep heavy reads OFF the loop (the dashboard already offloads board/semantic/signals/patterns/words to query-worker.mjs with TTLs; do not add synchronous scans) and keep poll load low (intervals 8/15/30/60s + SSE); (2) edge-cache the immutable statics so re-fetch storms stop queueing -- docker/Caddyfile now sets Cache-Control immutable for content-hashed /assets/* and a 1-day TTL for /favicon*. Note: /global/event in the log is an SSE stream (duration = connection lifetime); sentinel T4 now EXCLUDES it so it cannot cry-wolf the watchdog. The genuinely OURS endpoints have TTLs, and the one external call (/api/balance) has a 10s timeout. Validate a Caddyfile edit with: docker compose --project-directory docker exec caddy caddy validate --config /etc/caddy/Caddyfile

title: Nebula peer tunnel flapping (NEBULA-1)
purpose: Turn sentinel T8 'N tunnel-flap events' into a fix. The NEBULA-1 investigation proved the nebula PROCESS is healthy (systemd NRestarts=0, one stable PID); the recurring event is a peer/lighthouse tunnel teardown + re-handshake (`Close tunnel received, tearing down.` / `Taking new handshake` / `tunnelCheck state:dead`), typically to lighthouse-01 (vpnIp 10.100.0.1). This is a network/link problem, NOT a systemd restart problem -- do not rate-limit systemd.
commands: bash scripts/nebula-systemd-override.sh --diagnose   # classify restart-churn vs tunnel-flap + count it
python3 scripts/nebula-restart-trace.py --watch 60   # confirm it is not the process restarting
python3 scripts/triage-alerts.py   # group the T8 flags + de-dupe the stable key
journalctl -u nebula --since '-15min' | grep -E 'Close tunnel|Taking new handshake|state:dead'
note: Root cause lives in the peer/lighthouse repo (proxmox-dual-plane-mesh) -- this repo only watches and hands off. The handshake log shows UDP to 192.168.4.45:4242 and 100.70.43.78:4242 with `tunnelCheck state:dead` on vpnIp 10.100.0.1; check the lighthouse's UDP reachability (firewall/NAT/MTU) and the peer's reload cadence. A systemd drop-in (nebula-systemd-override.sh --apply) does NOT fix this: it only bounds restarts that are not happening. Threshold is SENTINEL_TUNNEL_MIN (default 4 flap events per sweep).

title: Stand up Grafana + SQLite (non-bespoke ops view)
purpose: One command to bring the Grafana + SQLite observability view (RULE #67) up on the host; it reads the two stores read-only, so it can never disagree with the source of truth.
note: Provisioned: dashboard 'opencode — cost, sessions, flags' (docker/grafana/provisioning/dashboards/opencode.json) + two SQLite datasources (../datasources/sqlite.yaml). Open http://127.0.0.1:3000 (anonymous viewer, localhost). If a datasource errors, check the plugin id frser-sqlite-datasource and the jsonData path key against the installed plugin version. Port: GF_PORT (default 3000); grafana-up.sh auto-picks a free port if the default is taken and names the holder (free-port.sh --owner). Tips: port 3000 is held by a FOREIGN node process (pid varies) -- see docs/known-ports.md; grafana-up auto-picks the next free port. If the host port does not answer but the container is healthy, check 'docker port opencode-grafana'.

title: Audit the BTRFS snapshot system (is it costing us?)
purpose: snapper-on-BTRFS root (/.snapshots/NNNN/snapshot): check retention limits, space pinned by CoW, whether qgroups/quota are enabled, and whether locate indexes every snapshot. Read-only; prints the tuning commands.
commands: sudo bash scripts/locate-prune-snapshots.sh --disable-timer   # if locate is not needed
sudo bash scripts/locate-prune-snapshots.sh --enable-timer   # re-enable the timer
note: Snapshots do not slow the OS by existing, but three costs are real: (1) locate/updatedb indexing /.snapshots bloats mlocate.db and is slow on a USB-HDD root -- add /.snapshots to PRUNEPATHS, then sudo updatedb; (2) CoW snapshots pin old blocks and fragment writes; (3) BTRFS qgroups (btrfs quota) are a known snapper drag -- sudo btrfs quota disable / removes it. Cap retention: sudo snapper -c root set-config TIMELINE_LIMIT_HOURLY=6 TIMELINE_LIMIT_DAILY=7 TIMELINE_LIMIT_WEEKLY=4 TIMELINE_LIMIT_MONTHLY=2 TIMELINE_LIMIT_YEARLY=0, NUMBER_LIMIT=20, then sudo snapper -c root cleanup number. Keep btrfs balance rare on a USB HDD. Note: the host lockup was CPU starvation, not disk. The locate fix is scripted: locate-prune-snapshots.sh (idempotent, backs up /etc/updatedb.conf, runs updatedb). Live: a plocate rebuild ran 76+ min reading 3.7GB (docker overlay2, ~1400 files/s) -- if locate is not essential, disable the updatedb timer instead of rebuilding. On a slow USB-HDD root, prefer on-demand search over maintaining the locate index: fd (installed) or scripts/ffind.sh (fd->find fallback); the updatedb timer is disabled.

title: Start the dev-loop progress-review timer (host)
purpose: Install + enable the user-level systemd timer that runs progress-review.sh every 15 min: it records a durable PASS row on a rev/gate advance and a FAIL row when the loop stalls. No sudo (user timer).
note: Install once FROM THE HOST repo -- the timer must run where the repo + store live (this sandbox has no systemd). progress-review reads next-action (git rev, last-gate, next queue unit) and logs to the observability ledger with stable keys progress-advance-<rev>/progress-stall-<rev>, so a persisting stall is ONE row. NOTIFY_WEBHOOK (if set in .env.local) gets a push on a stall. Pair with the sentinel timer (health, 5 min) + this (progression, 15 min). Uninstall: bash scripts/progress-review-install.sh --uninstall.
